A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FlexEvent research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison despite changes in pagination and presentation.

before.justification: V2 reports original object-detection results on three DSEC benchmarks, together with frequency, efficiency, ablation, and qualitative experiments in Section 4 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experimental results and adds qualitative examples. Its empirical content extends beyond results attributed to other papers.

M1.justification: The RVT/ResNet-50 branches, FlexFuse aggregation and gating, regularization, and FlexTune pseudo-label refinement and self-training procedures remain unchanged. Displaying existing losses as numbered equations does not introduce new method components.

E1.justification: Both versions use DSEC-Det, DSEC-Detection, and DSEC-MOD with the same detection categories and frequency conditions, including empty-event examples. Additional qualitative images illustrate existing driving scenarios rather than introducing distinct task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds a quantitative HDI-Former comparison, previously mentioned without a result row. Table 2 adds SENet, CBAM, ECA-Net, SAGate, DCF, SPNet, RAMNet, FAGC, EFNet, and DRFuser on DSEC-Detection. Several already appeared on DSEC-MOD, but their participation in this comparison is new. These additions substantially broaden the comparator set.

E3.justification: The reported dataset splits, COCO AP metrics, temporal-offset testing and label interpolation, training settings, and efficiency measurement procedures are retained. The added comparator rows do not document a revised evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Figure 5 adds two qualitative driving-scene comparisons, and Figure 7 adds a second frequency-dependent RVT/FlexEvent example. These additional images are distinct from the earlier appendix examples. Existing component ablations, hyperparameter analyses, and appendix robustness analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed or repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. No statistical reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Additional baseline scores and qualitative examples are reported. HDI-Former now has 46.7 mAP and 69.1 AP50 in Table 1, becoming the strongest listed baseline there. Existing scores remain unchanged, including FlexEvent's 57.4, 47.4, and 36.9 in Tables 1–3 and the appendix ablation results.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and reasoning are retained. Existing inline FlexTune losses become displayed Equations 8–9, and the appendix AP equation is renumbered from 8 to 10; their mathematical content is unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about adaptive fusion, frequency-adaptive learning, benchmark superiority, and operation up to 180 Hz. The introduction's numerical improvement claims are also unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations of fusion benefits, frequency generalization, and pseudo-label refinement are retained. Appendix D preserves the same limitations concerning sensor quality, unseen environments, and computational requirements.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, preprocessing, and appendix resource links remain unchanged. Code availability moves from an abstract statement to the front-page 'Project Page & Code' label at the same project address, without establishing changed access.

R1.justification: V3 adds Munir et al. (2023), cited for DRFuser, and explicitly cites RVT for the event representation in Section 3.1. The related-work discussion and substantive novelty positioning otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 updates affiliations and conference information, adds acknowledgments, removes duplicated wording in Section 4.2, and makes small grammatical and tense corrections. The section organization and most prose are retained.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 expand and clarify best/second-best highlighting. Figures 5 and 7 are enlarged and rearranged with additional panels. Captions, numerical formatting, equation display, and page flow receive localized adjustments; most figures and appendix displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The added HDI-Former row repairs a missing quantitative comparison, Table 2 supplies broader baseline context, and additional qualitative cases modestly strengthen the evidence. However, the introduction's unchanged 15.5-point lead over the previous best is inconsistent with the expanded Table 1: 57.4 versus 46.7 implies 10.7 points. The gains improve completeness but leave this summary claim unreconciled.
